jobs.title: Sr Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
About The Role

Uber is launching AV Labs to accelerate the autonomous technology ecosystem. We're building out a high-velocity team of multi-disciplinary experts to turn real-world operations into high-quality data for our autonomous partners. This team is focused on the hardest problem in AV today: unlocking real-world, long-tail driving data. Autonomy is now a data race—and Uber has an edge: We collect rare, real-world driving data at a scale and capital efficiency no one else can match.

As a Senior ML Engineer, you will be at the forefront of Physical AI
, building advanced autonomy algorithms and models to add rich semantics to our massive driving data. You will be responsible for the development and implementation of the latest machine learning techniques that enables better data mining, deep scene understanding, and causal modeling of ego vehicle behavior. The ideal candidate will be able to identify complex edge cases, provide robust algorithmic solutions, and set a high technical excellence bar.

What The Candidate Will Do

Algorithm Development: Lead the development of autonomy algorithms and foundation models that extract high-fidelity semantic meaning from complex urban edge cases to enrich our L4 data lake.
Systems Architecture Design: Architect scalable ML systems, including management of upstream sensor dependencies.
Technical Leadership: Partner with fellow engineers to architect, design, and build scalable solutions for ML technology that can stand the test of scale and availability.
Dataset Optimization: Deliver high-quality datasets to accelerate ML technologies through advanced sensor data collection, processing, and auto-labeling.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with platform, product, and security engineering teams to enable the successful deployment of the latest machine learning techniques into production.

Basic Qualifications

4+ years of working experience in the ML/Robotics industry.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related fields.
Proficient in Python and Linux environments.
Familiar with modern AI/ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in the Autonomous Driving domain.
Proven track record of deploying ML models in safety-critical physical systems.
Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Vision, Robotics, or Machine Learning.
Familiarity with C++ and high-performance computing.

For Sunnyvale, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $202,000 per year - USD $224,000 per year.

You will be eligible to participate in Uber's bonus program, and may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits.

Ready to Ride?

This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook — it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves — we'd love to hear from you.

You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.

Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in-office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role's requirements.

Uber is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing this form.

jobs.title: Staff AI/ML Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Description

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.

Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.

Role

As a Staff AI/ML Engineer in the Embodied AI organization, you will serve as a senior individual contributor developing and deploying machine learning solutions that directly impact autonomous driving performance. You will design and implement advanced ML models that enable safe and reliable vehicle behavior across diverse real-world scenarios.

In this role, you will partner closely with cross-functional engineering teams, contribute to core technical direction within your domain, and support the growth of engineers through technical collaboration and mentorship. You will help translate research into scalable onboard ML solutions while contributing to the continuous improvement of our autonomy stack.

What You'll Do

Design and implement ML solutions aligned with GM’s autonomous driving objectives.
Apply techniques such as unsupervised pre-training, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, model scaling/selection, foundation modeling, to solve problems in object detection/tracking/classification, trajectory generation, and safe AI.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deploy models and algorithms into onboard driving systems.
Contribute to applied research efforts and remain current with advancements in ML frameworks and methods.
Design and build efficient infrastructure, pipelines, and tooling to facilitate fast-pace model iterations.
Drive technical execution from prototyping through production deployment, documenting learnings and best practices.
Support and mentor engineers through technical collaboration and code reviews, fostering knowledge sharing and engineering excellence.

Your Skills & Abilities

Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or related field.
Experience working with large-scale foundation models and alignment methods applied to real-world systems.
Demonstrated ability to deliver applied ML solutions under real-world constraints and timelines.
Proficiency in PyTorch and Python.
Experience building and scaling model training pipelines enabling efficient iteration across teams.
Strong data processing skills using tools such as NumPy, Pandas, and Apache Spark.
Strong communication skills enabling effective collaboration across engineering teams.
Experience deploying ML models into production environments and understanding end-to-end deployment workflows.
Experience in robotics or autonomous driving systems preferred.

Remote: This role is based remotely but if you live within a 50-mile radius of Austin, Detroit, Warren, Milford or Mountain View, you are expected to report to that location three times per week, at minimum.

Compensation : The compensation information is a good faith estimate only. It is based on what a successful applicant might be paid in accordance with applicable state laws. The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of the California Bay Area.

The salary range for this role is $212,800.00 to $305,300.00. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.
Bonus Potential: An incentive pay program offers payouts based on company performance, job level, and individual performance.

Benefits:

Benefits: GM offers a variety of health and wellbeing benefit programs. Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plan, sickness and accident benefits, life insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, employee assistance program, GM vehicle discounts and more.

This job may be eligible for relocation benefits.

Company Vehicle: Upon successful completion of a motor vehicle report review, you will be eligible to participate in a company vehicle evaluation program, through which you will be assigned a General Motors vehicle to drive and evaluate. Note: program participants are required to purchase/lease a qualifying GM vehicle every four years unless one of a limited number of exceptions applies.

jobs.description:
Responsibilities

About the Role
ByteDance’s Dev Infra team is looking for talented Machine Learning Engineers to join our Dev AI initiative. Our mission is to build intelligent systems that transform how engineers design, develop, test, debug, and maintain software at scale.

In this role, you will work at the intersection of machine learning, large language models, code intelligence, and developer infrastructure. You will develop and improve AI systems for code generation, automated testing, debugging, code understanding, and agentic software engineering, with the goal of significantly improving developer productivity across ByteDance.

Responsibilities:
- Develop and improve machine learning and large language model systems for software engineering tasks, including code generation, unit test generation, and debugging.
- Build AI-powered developer agents and intelligent workflows that can reason over large codebases, interact with development environments and tools, execute multi-step engineering tasks, and assist engineers throughout the software development lifecycle.
- Improve model and agent performance through prompt engineering, context engineering, retrieval, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, tool-use design, and agent harness engineering.
- Build high-quality training and evaluation data pipelines for software engineering tasks, including data collection, filtering, synthesis, labeling, and hard-example mining.
- Explore and apply advances in large language models, code intelligence, program analysis, reinforcement learning, and autonomous software engineering to real-world developer productivity problems at scale.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree or above in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Software Engineering, or a related field.
- 5+ years of relevant industry or research experience in machine learning, large language models, code intelligence, AI-powered developer tools, or related areas.
- Strong programming skills in one or more languages such as Python, Go, Java, C++, JavaScript, or TypeScript.
- Solid understanding of data structures, algorithms, machine learning, operating systems, databases, and fundamental system design principles.
- Experience owning complex machine learning projects end-to-end, from problem formulation and data construction to model development, evaluation, deployment, and production iteration.
- Strong system design and engineering skills, with experience building scalable, reliable, and efficient machine learning systems or AI-powered applications.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to drive complex technical projects across teams.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience building or leading AI systems for software engineering, including code generation, coding agents, unit test generation, debugging, or code review.
- Deep experience with large language models and one or more model improvement or post-training techniques, such as supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, preference optimization, prompt engineering, context engineering, retrieval, or model evaluation.
- Experience designing and improving agentic systems, including tool-using LLMs, coding agents, agent harnesses, MCP, agent skills, planning, memory, or multi-step execution workflows.
- Experience building large-scale training data, evaluation datasets, benchmarks, or experimentation pipelines for machine learning or code intelligence systems.
- Strong understanding of software engineering and code intelligence techniques such as program analysis, compilers, static analysis, code search, repository indexing, testing, and debugging.
- Publications, patents, open-source contributions, or demonstrated technical leadership in machine learning, large language models, code intelligence, developer tools, or AI for software engineering.

Why Join ByteDance

Inspiring creativity is at the core of ByteDance's mission. Our innovative products are built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Together, we create value for our communities, inspire creativity and enrich life - a mission we work towards every day.​
As ByteDancers, we strive to do great things with great people. We lead with curiosity, humility, and a desire to make impact in a rapidly growing tech company. By constantly iterating and fostering an "Always Day 1" mindset, we achieve meaningful breakthroughs for ourselves, our Company, and our users. When we create and grow together, the possibilities are limitless. Join us.​
Diversity & Inclusion​
ByteDance is committed to creating an inclusive space where employees are valued for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. Our platform connects people from across the globe and so does our workplace. At ByteDance, our mission is to inspire creativity and enrich life. To achieve that goal, we are committed to celebrating our diverse voices and to creating an environment that reflects the many communities we reach. We are passionate about this and hope you are too.​

If you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation, please reach out to us at https://tinyurl.com/RA-request​

jobs.title: Principal Applied AI Engineer / Forward-Deployed Engineer - Remote (San Francisco Bay Area)
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Principal Applied AI Engineer / Forward-Deployed Engineer based in San Francisco Bay Area.

As a Principal Applied AI Engineer, you will play a key role in designing and delivering practical AI-powered solutions that address real-world business challenges. You will work directly with business stakeholders and clients to identify opportunities, translate complex needs into technical solutions, and lead projects from initial discovery through production deployment. Combining strong software engineering expertise with advanced knowledge of large language models, you will build intelligent workflows, AI agents, and enterprise applications. You will also drive the integration of AI technologies with business platforms, APIs, and secure data environments. This hands-on position offers significant technical ownership and autonomy in a fully remote, fast-paced environment. Your work will help organizations become more connected, efficient, and intelligent through responsible AI innovation.

Accountabilities

Lead the development and implementation of production-ready AI applications, working closely with clients, internal teams, and business stakeholders to transform operational challenges into scalable, secure, and effective technical solutions.

Own the full development lifecycle of AI-powered solutions, from business discovery and requirements gathering to prototyping, development, testing, deployment, and ongoing maintenance.
Collaborate directly with clients, business teams, and leadership to identify opportunities and translate business requirements into practical AI applications.
Design, build, and deploy AI-assisted workflows, intelligent agents, and applications using large language models and modern development frameworks.
Integrate AI models and services with Google Workspace, Gemini Enterprise, internal systems, APIs, and approved external data sources.
Develop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems and other data retrieval approaches that enable applications to access and use relevant business information.
Implement secure data access mechanisms, permissions, tool calling, and integrations that respect organizational and client-specific access controls.
Establish reliable application architectures with appropriate testing, monitoring, error handling, and performance optimization.
Evaluate AI models, development tools, and cloud services, balancing functionality, reliability, privacy, security, and operating costs.
Gather stakeholder feedback, troubleshoot technical issues, and continuously improve applications following production launches.
Create reusable technical patterns, document development approaches, and share knowledge to support future engineering initiatives.
Monitor emerging developments in applied AI, LLMs, AI agents, frameworks, and related technologies to identify opportunities for innovation.
Identify ways to incorporate AI into internal operations and client-facing solutions while promoting a human-centered approach to technology.
Deliver key initial milestones within the first 90 days, including one useful internal AI-powered workflow, one client-relevant demonstration, and documented technical patterns covering testing, permissions, reliability, and performance.

Requirements

You are a highly experienced software engineer with a strong background in applied AI development and a proven ability to turn experimental concepts into reliable production applications. You combine technical depth with practical problem-solving skills, communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, and are comfortable taking ownership of complex projects in fast-moving environments.

8+ years of software engineering experience or equivalent hands-on engineering expertise, including recent experience developing LLM-powered applications.
Strong proficiency in Python or TypeScript.
Hands-on experience building, integrating, and deploying applications using APIs and cloud-based services.
Demonstrated experience developing AI-powered applications, workflows, and agents using large language models (LLMs).
Practical experience implementing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), data retrieval, tool calling, and other common LLM application patterns.
Proven ability to take AI-powered applications from prototype to production and provide ongoing support after deployment.
Strong understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including application architecture, testing, CI/CD, and deployment practices.
Experience integrating applications with enterprise platforms, business systems, APIs, and external data sources.
Knowledge of data permissions, security, privacy, and responsible management of sensitive company and client information.
Ability to design reliable applications with effective monitoring, error handling, and performance management.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with the capacity to work independently, make sound technical decisions, and navigate ambiguity.
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and taking projects from initial ideas to fully functioning production solutions.
Experience with modern AI coding tools and the ability to incorporate them effectively into development workflows.

Candidates should also be prepared to discuss an AI-powered application they personally built and launched, explaining the original business problem, technical architecture, development and deployment process, testing approach, challenges encountered, and improvements made after launch.

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance plans, with options available to suit individual needs.
Paid sick time and 10 paid holidays.
Flexible vacation policy that supports work-life balance and personal well-being.

jobs.description:
"The best way to predict the future is to invent it." Alan Kay

Imagine taking a platform that already serves hundreds of thousands of companies, already turns a profit and already grows quickly, and then deciding to rebuild the whole thing around AI agents. Not a side project. Not an innovation lab tucked away in a corner. The entire product.

That is exactly what this team is doing, and they want four exceptional Staff and Principal engineers in the room while it happens.

Our client is a profitable, venture-backed AI go-to-market platform headquartered in San Francisco. Revenue teams use it to find the right buyers, start the right conversations and close more deals, powered by one of the largest B2B data sets in the market. Around 250 people, founded over a decade ago, and still moving with the urgency of a Series A. If you have ever wanted genuine scale and genuine momentum in the same job, this is a rare overlap.

The role in one breath

You'll be the senior IC people look for when the problem is hard, ambiguous and expensive to get wrong. You'll own the architecture for a meaningful slice of the platform, either the large-scale distributed systems underneath it or the agent-centric AI products on top, and you'll move between the highest-priority initiatives alongside VPs and the C-suite. Engineering here is expected to shape revenue, not just close tickets.

What you'll be doing

Setting technical direction
for a major area of the platform, from data model to deployment, and backing those choices with clear reasoning.
Taking on the gnarliest problems first:
build versus buy, cost versus latency, consistency versus throughput. The calls you make will ripple through the whole engineering organisation.
Designing agentic systems that hold up in production.
LLM orchestration, tool use, retrieval over a very large data set, evaluation loops and the unglamorous plumbing that makes agents reliable rather than merely impressive in a demo.
Scaling the core.
High-volume OLTP workloads, search and indexing at serious scale, and pipelines that keep hundreds of thousands of customers supplied with fresh, accurate data.
Raising the bar across teams
with standards, patterns and reviews that make every engineer around you faster.
Working AI-first yourself.
Agents and AI coding tools are part of how this team designs, investigates and ships every day, and you'll help define what great looks like.

The tech

Languages and frameworks:
Ruby and Ruby on Rails, Python, React
Data:
MongoDB, Elasticsearch, large-scale OLTP and data pipelines
Infrastructure:
Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, Google Cloud Platform
AI:
LLM-based systems, agent frameworks, retrieval and evaluation tooling
How you build:
Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code and similar AI-assisted tools, used daily

You don't need every item on day one. Deep strength in distributed systems or LLM-based products, with genuine curiosity about the other half, matters far more than ticking boxes. (Ruby and Mongo are bonuses, not gatekeepers.)

What the hiring team is looking for

This is where we'll be precise, because the hiring team has been very clear about what lands.

Must-haves

8 to 15 years
in backend or full-stack engineering, with real time spent building large-scale distributed systems.
You've owned and operated systems at scale
, serving 100K+ users, and lived with them in production, pager and all.
Strong system design for large-scale data and distributed systems.
You can sketch the architecture, then explain exactly where it will break.
A big tech and startup blend.
Big tech experience is welcome, and you'll also have at least one stint at a reputable high-growth startup (pre-seed to Series D), an AI-native company or a founding engineering team.
A clear upward trajectory.
Your scope has grown with each move, and you've held a Staff-level (or higher) title for a year or more.
Hands-on LLM experience or serious OLTP scale.
The strongest candidates have built LLM-based systems in production, scaled large transactional databases, or both.
Based in the San Francisco Bay Area
and happy to be in the SF office three days a week.

The profile that really shines

The hiring team particularly loves engineers currently at a reputable, high-growth company who bring either a strong database background or production LLM work. A former data engineer who has branched out into distributed systems and AI is a standout archetype here.

Nice to have

Ruby on Rails, Python, MongoDB or Elasticsearch in production
Daily, hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools, with a story about how they changed the way you ship
A strong CS degree (far less important once you have five or more years of excellent work behind you)

A quick note on fit

To save everyone time: this seat is for builders of core platforms and AI products, so forward-deployed engineering backgrounds aren't the target. Long tenures where scope stayed flat, or a pattern of very short stints, tend not to progress either. If your career shows steady growth and real ownership, you're exactly who we want to hear from.

Why engineers say yes

Scale you can feel.
Your work reaches hundreds of thousands of companies and millions of users from your first week.
A rebuild, not a maintenance job.
Rebuilding a profitable product around agents is the rarest kind of greenfield: real users, real data, real stakes.
A seat at the table.
You'll work directly with engineering and product leadership, and your architectural calls will shape the business.
Autonomy and ownership.
A culture built on extreme ownership, bold experimentation and continuous learning.
Profitable and growing.
The freedom to make long-term technical bets without runway anxiety.

The package

Base salary up to $412K
, depending on level (Staff or Principal)
Meaningful equity
plus annual bonus
Hybrid:
three days a week in the San Francisco office
Visa transfers welcome
(including H-1B transfers and OPT)
A focused four-step interview process
centred on your real experience and how you solve problems
Four openings
, so there is genuine room for more than one great engineer

Ready to build what comes next?

If you've scaled distributed systems, shipped LLM-powered products and want your next role to define an AI-native platform at serious scale, we'd love to talk.

Hit apply with your resume and tell us about the largest system you've owned and the most interesting thing you've built with LLMs. Every application is read by a real recruiter at Big Wave Digital, and we'll be in touch quickly if there's a match.

jobs.description:
The Company

PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Job Summary:

Venmo is hiring Staff Data Scientists across Core Experiences, Consumer Financial Services (CFS), and Commerce. Core Experiences includes payments, requests, the social feed, notifications, search, and network growth. CFS includes products such as the Venmo debit card and funds-in. Commerce focuses on business payments and helping merchants grow.

As a senior data science leader, you’ll help shape Venmo’s growth strategy by finding and sizing opportunities and deciding what to measure, test, and build. You’ll partner with business, product, engineering, risk, and other teams, and develop scalable approaches to experimentation and measurement, including causal inference, social and network effects, forecasting, and engagement. You’ll translate complex data into clear insights that guide product, design, and investment decisions for a leading payments app.

Job Description:

Essential Responsibilities:

Lead and manage data science projects, ensuring timely delivery and alignment with business goals.
Develop and maintain data models, algorithms, and reporting systems to support data analysis and decision-making.
Analyze complex datasets to identify trends, patterns, and insights that drive strategic initiatives.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand data needs and provide actionable insights.
Ensure data quality and integrity through regular audits and validation processes.
Mentor and guide junior data scientists, fostering a culture of continuous learning and improvement.

Minimum Qualifications:

5+ years relevant experience and a Bachelor’s degree OR Any equivalent combination of education and experience.

Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Qualifications:

Essential Responsibilities:

Lead data science for your area, setting the analytical strategy and ensuring timely delivery aligned with product and business goals.
Design and analyze complex experiments, including tests where one person's experience affects their friends, tests in a two-sided network, and tests with small samples or long-term outcomes, and define the guardrails that protect payments and trust.
Define the metrics, funnels, and models that follow people and businesses from first use to lasting engagement, including activation, retention, and healthy engagement for a payments app.
Measure how new features and broad changes affect people, separating real behavior change from novelty and clicks.
Uncover what drives user and business behavior across Venmo, such as how the social feed, notifications, search, payments, financial products, and merchant experiences help people connect, pay, and manage money.
Build modeling frameworks, leveraging machine learning, statistics, and optimization, to solve propensity modeling problems and other related product problems.
Apply classic machine learning algorithms, such as regression, tree-based models (random forests, gradient boosting) and clustering, to propensity, segmentation, churn and forecasting problems.
Develop forecasts and growth models with Finance and Product, and recommend where to invest next.
Collaborate with Product, Design, Engineering, and Finance to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations, with an honest view of confidence and risk.
Build and own AI-native data science workflows: agents, skills and context layers for instrumentation, analysis, experiment readouts and data quality checks, with clear boundaries between trusted automation and expert judgment.
Measure the quality and impact of AI and agentic product experiences, combining product metrics with model-quality and evaluation signals.
Help lead how AI makes data science faster at Venmo, from instrumentation to analysis and data quality checks.
Ensure data quality and integrity by validating instrumentation and experiment results before decisions are made.
Mentor and guide data scientists, and set the bar for analytical rigor across the team.

Minimum Qualifications:

5 years of relevant experience and a Bachelor’s degree OR Any equivalent combination of education and experience.
5 years of experience in experimentation, causal inference, and statistical methods
5 years of experience using SQL and at least one scripting language: Python or R, for processing large, complex, and messy datasets.
3 years of experience designing and reading out A/B Testing or hypothesis testing to inform product decisions and new experience launches
3 years of experience partnering with leadership engineers, product managers, and data engineers to understand business needs and how these can be addressed through analytics
3 years of experience translating complex problems into simpler terms, and effectively influencing both peers and senior leadership (3 years).

Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree with at least 8 years of professional experience, or a master’s degree with at least 6 years of experience.
Advanced proficiency in SQL and strong Python or R for large-scale transaction and event data, forecasting, experimentation, and causal inference.
Deep experience in end-to-end product experimentation, including test design, power analysis, small-sample and long-horizon tests, and decision-ready readouts. Experience with network effects, social products, marketplaces, two-sided platforms, recommendations, or notification and engagement systems.
Experience with consumer financial products or analytics for payments, cards, deposits, or credit, or with merchant and small business analytics.
Experience building forecasts, growth models, or predictive models (including machine learning) that a business used to plan or make decisions.
Experience with agentic analytics and AI-enabled data science workflows, including leveraging AI and LLM-based tools and agents to speed up analysis, instrumentation, experimentation, and data quality checks.
Highly skilled with agentic coding tools and workflows (for example, Claude Code or Cursor) to speed up analysis and production code.
Ability to translate complex analyses into clear insights and recommendations for technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with experience influencing senior leaders on investment and roadmap decisions and partnering across Product, Design, Finance, Engineering, and Analytics. Ability to independently lead complex analytical projects, identify measurement gaps, and recommend improvements to product and business strategy, while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Collaborative team player who builds trust across functions, shares knowledge openly, and puts team and Venmo outcomes ahead of individual credit.
Strong ownership and commitment: follows through on commitments, raises risks early, and stays accountable for results from first analysis through business impact.
Consistent record of delivering high-quality work on time, including through ambiguity and shifting priorities, and of making clear trade-offs to protect what matters most.

jobs.title: Staff Technologist-AI Architect
jobs.description:
Staff Technologist-AI Architect

Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG)
builds the products that power infrastructure, solutions, and data management our customers need most. Our teams design and develop the hardware and software that connect infrastructure, accelerate computational workloads, integrate across the stack, protect data continuity, and deliver the platforms, applications, and diagnostics our customers rely on every day at enterprise scale.

Some product builders follow the rules. Ours rewrite them.

Within ISG, innovation isn't just about creating new technology- it's about challenging assumptions and reimagining how work gets done. Engineers define intent, author precise specifications, and orchestrate AI agents that execute at speed and scale. AI is embedded throughout our development process, helping us move faster, learn quicker, and deliver greater impact. Yet the most important contribution remains uniquely human: deciding what to build, designing how it should work, and applying the judgment needed to earn our customers' trust. When your products power critical infrastructure around the world, that responsibility matters.

We move quickly toward the work that matters most. We reward experimentation, encourage bold thinking, and remove unnecessary barriers so great ideas can become reality faster. Our teams embrace a customer-first, first-to-market mindset, transforming rapid feedback into better products and better outcomes. We aren't looking for people who are content with the status quo- we look for builders who question it, improve it, and occasionally rewrite it.

If you're energized by solving complex systems challenges, excited to work alongside AI to amplify your impact, and motivated by the opportunity to shape what's next instead of simply maintaining what's been done before, you'll find your place here.
From applied research to advanced engineering, the Engineering Technologist team has the expertise to
shape ground-breaking products, material and processes. It's a fascinating field of work. We're involved in
assessing the competition, developing technology and product strategies and generating intellectual
property. We lead technology investigations, analyze industry capabilities and recommend potential
acquisitions or vendor partner opportunities. Our insights influence product architecture and definitions.
And we work with colleagues across the business to ensure our products always lead the way.

Join us as a Staff Technologist-AI Architect
on our ISG-CTO
team
in Santa Clara, California
to do the best work of your career and make a profound social impact.

What you'll achieve

As a Staff Technologist-AI Architect

jobs.title: AI Research Scientist, Materials Discovery
jobs.description:
At Logical Intelligence, our mission is to accelerate the discovery of materials that make the next generation of technology possible, from light emitters and semiconductors to batteries, electric vehicles, and the chips behind AI and robotics. Large language models alone are not enough to get there. Discovering new materials requires an understanding of chemistry and physics to guide the search, and energy-based models let us build that understanding directly into our discovery loop. We work closely with industry and lab partners to shorten the path from research to real products.

About the Role

As a Research Scientist
, you will join an interdisciplinary team of quantum chemists, physicists, ML scientists, and engineers, where the biggest impact comes from working together. You'll develop the AI models that drive our discovery loop, proposing novel molecules that are then synthesized and tested in our partner labs, and you'll see your predictions confronted with real measurements.

What You’ll Do

Tackle the core research problems in our discovery loop: how to generate promising candidates, screen them reliably, and decide which molecules are worth testing next.
Own model evaluation, including benchmarks on held-out chemical families, accuracy against both quantum-chemistry calculations and experiment, calibration of uncertainty estimates, prospective tests where the model predicts before the lab measures, and tracking across model versions.
Compare AI predictions with measurements, investigate disagreements, and turn what you learn into concrete model changes, in collaboration with chemists, AI researchers and engineers.
Design experiments with our partner labs so that each round of synthesis and testing is as informative as possible.

You Will Thrive in This Role If You Have

A PhD in machine learning or a Master’s or Bachelor’s with relevant industry experience
Working knowledge in energy-based models, diffusion or score-based models, or similar generative approaches, and an interest in going deeper
Knowledge of chemistry, or a genuine interest in learning it working alongside our chemists.
Experience designing evaluations and experiments that correlate with downstream performance
A strong record of impactful research, shown through publications, open-source software
Excellent scientific writing and communication, and comfort working in an interdisciplinary team.

Especially Strong Candidates May Also Have

Hands-on research experience with energy-based models, or with methods that combine learning with search and optimization.
Experience with molecular ML, such as property prediction, generative molecular design, ML interatomic potentials, or quantum-chemistry workflows (e.g. DFT).
Experience with closed-loop design using real lab feedback

jobs.description:

About StackOne

StackOne is the integration infrastructure for AI agents. Backed by GV and Workday Ventures ($24M raised), we make it possible for any AI agent — whether our customers build it into their product or buy it off the shelf — to take real action across the enterprise stack. Our platform gives agents 630+ connectors and 43,000+ pre-built actions, an AI connector builder for everything not covered yet, and the production layer agents actually need: semantic tool discovery that cuts token use by up to 80%, managed authentication and per-action permissions, the most accurate prompt injection defense on the market, and end-to-end observability.

Join us on our fast trajectory to build the future of agentic integrations.

About The Role

We're hiring our first Forward Deployed Engineer
to help our customers decide where AI agents will make a measurable difference to their business, and then make sure it happens.

You'll sit with executives and their teams, learn how the business runs day to day, and turn that into an AI strategy and rollout plan tied to the number they care about, whether that's hours saved, cost per process or revenue. You'll design the agents, guide our Solutions Engineers as they build them, and stay with the customer until the agreed results are in. We're starting with healthcare, our fastest-growing vertical. Knowing its systems, its data and its compliance rules will be a big part of the job.

You'll report to our CEO & Co-Founder, and work from our San Mateo office 1 to 2 days a week, with regular travel to customer sites across the US.

What You’ll Be Doing

Run discovery with C-level leaders, managers and their teams: walk through their processes, map workflows and data, and find what AI agents can automate or improve.
Build a strategy and rollout plan for each customer, tied to the metric their business cares about, and present it to their leadership.
Design the agents, skills and plugins that deliver the plan, including inside tools like Microsoft Copilot, Glean and Gemini Enterprise, and steer the Solutions Engineers who build and maintain them.

Hands-on experience building and deploying AI agents (with agent SDKs or via low code platforms), and ways of optimising and measuring accuracy & efficiency of agentic workflows, enough to judge what's worth building and to review someone else's build. jobs.title: Data Scientist, Discovery & Recommendations
jobs.description:
About Us

Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.

We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process.

About The Team

Twitch is all about community, and our Community team is a core pillar of what makes Twitch, Twitch. Community Discovery & ML (CDML) helps millions of viewers find the creators and communities they'll love. That covers search, browse, the mobile live and clips feeds, recommended notifications, and the recommendation systems behind them. When a viewer finds a new creator through one of these, it's often the start of a lasting connection. That connection is what keeps viewers, and the creators they watch, coming back.

About The Role

We're looking for a data scientist with strong statistics and modeling skills to be the science partner for the machine learning and recommendation systems behind Twitch's discovery products. You will work with product managers, ML engineers and applied scientists to help build what our recommendation systems should optimize for. That means balancing what a viewer does today (a click, a play, minutes watched) against what keeps them coming back: return visits, daily habits, and lasting connections with creators. It also means weighing short-form clips against long-form live content, and each surface against the others. This role will draw from a variety of statistical learning techniques, causal inference, optimization and recommender systems evaluation, and it still owns the full path from question to decision.

Reporting to the Director of Data Science, you will work from our San Francisco, CA office.

You Will:

Help define the objective functions and success metrics for ranking and recommendations across feeds, search and notifications. Make the trade-offs explicit between short-term engagement (clicks, plays, watch time) and long-term outcomes (return visits, retention, new creator connections), including how short-form clips and live content add to or take away from each other.
Evaluate ranking, recommendation and feed changes with ML engineers and applied scientists. This covers A/B tests and long-running holdouts, offline metrics that predict online results, and the cost and value of exploration and cold start. Handle the hard cases: novelty effects, interference between experiments, two-sided marketplace effects involving creators and viewers, and feedback loops in recommendation data.
Build statistical and ML models that explain viewer behavior and size opportunities, such as propensity, uplift, survival and retention models. Include proxy metrics that predict long-term retention, so teams can decide in days rather than months.
Turn ambiguous product questions into clear analyses. Quantify the uncertainty, and make recommendations that inform the machine learning and discovery roadmap.
Define the logging and data needed to measure discovery surfaces, and check its quality.
Contribute to the team's standards for experimentation, causal inference and model evaluation, and share what you learn with other data scientists.

You Have:

A BA/BS in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science or a related quantitative field, or equivalent industry experience.
3+ years as a data scientist in a high-velocity, data-driven environment, with hands-on experience applying statistical modeling and machine learning (regression, classification, causal inference, time series), including the assumptions behind each method and when it fails.
Experience designing and analyzing online experiments, including variance reduction, power analysis and the pitfalls of interpreting results.
Expert SQL and proficiency in Python or R.
A track record of using data and models to influence product decisions and leadership.

Bonus Points

An MS or PhD in a quantitative field.
Experience with recommender systems, search ranking or feed ranking, such as offline evaluation (precision and recall, NDCG), exploration versus exploitation, or cold-start problems.
Experience with multi-objective optimization or with defining objective functions for ranking systems, including choosing weights between competing goals.
Experience building proxy metrics for long-term outcomes, or estimating long-term effects from long-running holdouts or observational data (e.g., difference-in-differences, synthetic control, uplift modeling).
Experience with two-sided platforms or marketplaces, where changes for viewers also affect creators or supply.
Experience on a consumer content platform: streaming, short-form video, social or marketplaces.
Familiarity with Twitch, as a viewer or a creator (or both!).

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Solutions Architecture (SA) organization helps Stripe's most strategic customers design and validate technical solutions that drive their business forward. Within SA, our team builds the tools, workflows, and custom technical assets that make the broader SA org more effective—turning individual ingenuity into org-wide capability.

We are looking for AI Engineers who are energized by working close to the business and the users we serve. You'll operate as an embedded, high-context engineer focused on the highest-leverage opportunities across the SA org—building production-quality tooling, supporting our most strategic engagements, and shipping automation that meaningfully improves how Solutions Architects work every day.

What You'll Do

As an AI Engineer, you'll be embedded directly with the Solutions Architecture team—building alongside them, deeply understanding their workflows, and shipping tools and automation that permanently change how they operate. Your measure of success is SA productivity: the engagements you've accelerated, the workflows you've transformed, and the tools you've built that the org adopts as default.

You'll ship code daily. You'll discover where SAs lose time and build high-impact solutions. You'll take what works for one person and scale it to work for the org. And when our most strategic customer engagements need custom technical assets, you'll build those too.

This is a role for someone who wants to work at the intersection of engineering and business impact—close to customers, close to revenue, and building for people you can see using your work every day.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with Solutions Architects, SA leadership, Product, and Engineering to scope technical work and translate ambiguous business needs into well-defined deliverables
Evaluate and integrate AI capabilities (LLMs, agents, workflow automation) where they provide genuine leverage—not for novelty, but for measurable productivity improvement
Architect and build internal tools, agents, and automated workflows that accelerate SA and manager productivity across technical discovery, solution design, demoing, user engagements, territory/pipeline management, and product interlock
Take high-potential tools and workflows built by SAs and managers and harden them into scalable, maintainable, production-grade solutions
Identify patterns across SA workflows and proactively build solutions that address recurring friction
Build custom demo environments, PoC applications, and technical assets for Stripe's most strategic customer engagements
Document tools, architectures, and usage patterns so others can adopt and extend what you've built
Debug, extend, and maintain backend systems across a variety of codebases and infrastructure

Minimum Requirements

4+ years of experience as an engineer shipping production systems
Strong backend engineering fundamentals: you can debug a failing system, trace issues across services, and reason about data flows
Experience building and deploying AI agents, LLM-powered tools, or workflow automation beyond basic prompt engineering
Experience scoping and delivering work with minimal oversight in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment
Proficiency in at least two of: Ruby, Node.js, Python, or Next.js
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) including deployment, monitoring, and basic DevOps
Experience building internal tools, developer platforms, or workflow automation
Demonstrated ability to work across multiple codebases and technology stacks simultaneously
Hands-on experience using AI/LLM tools in your engineering workflow—you're fluent with AI-assisted development but not dependent on it; you can reason through problems and debug without AI as a crutch
Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can translate technical decisions for non-technical stakeholders and navigate cross-functional collaboration naturally
Comfort with ambiguity—you can take a loosely-defined business problem, scope the engineering work, and ship iteratively without waiting for a perfect spec

Preferred Qualifications

Experience designing systems that non-engineers can build on top of or extend themselves (e.g., platforms, low-code frameworks, template systems)
Experience in a Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or GTM Engineering role—or a product engineering role where you worked closely with customers or go-to-market teams
Familiarity with Stripe's products, APIs, or the payments/fintech domain
Experience integrating with third-party platforms (Salesforce, Gong, etc.)
Track record of building tools or systems that were adopted beyond your immediate team
Background in consulting, professional services, or other roles that blend technical depth with business context

Who You Are

Beyond the technical requirements, we're looking for a specific kind of engineer:

You want to be close to the business. You're energized by seeing your work directly impact how a sales team wins a deal or how a customer succeeds.
You're a pragmatic builder. You ship working solutions quickly, iterate based on real usage, and know when "good enough now" beats "perfect later." You'd rather show a working prototype today than present a roadmap deck next quarter.
You're a software engineer by practice. You can architect systems, debug production issues, write clean code, and reason about tradeoffs. AI is a tool in your belt, not a substitute for engineering judgment.
You're a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it generalizes. You think in reusable systems, not one-off scripts.
You thrive without a traditional product team structure. No PRDs landing in your lap, no dedicated PM, no sprint ceremonies. You identify the highest-leverage problem, scope the work, and ship it. You're comfortable trading on-call rotations and rigid processes for autonomy and impact.
You're a strong communicator. You can partner with SAs who are domain experts, understand their workflows deeply enough to build great tools, and explain your technical choices to leadership.

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Stripes on the Works in Progress team based in the London, UK office also work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

jobs.title: AI Research Computing Facilitator
jobs.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Position overview

About The Role

Stanford Research Computing is seeking an AI Research Computing Facilitator who will bring the perspective of the research community to the selection, support, and processes associated with enterprise and research focused AI platforms (eg. Claude for Education, ChatGPT, etc). The individual will provide feedback into choosing, evaluating, approving, supporting, and using AI tools that are of key importance to the Stanford research community and will have service ownership responsibilities associated with AI tools focused on research (eg. Claude Science, Rosalind, etc).

The SRC team runs large scale computing and data platforms and the successful candidate will support the deployment of AI tools in these environments ensuring alignment between campus research computing resources and enterprise AI tools owned by the UIT Enterprise Technologies (ET) AI team.

In this role you will interact directly with research teams but will also spend a significant amount of your time working with the UIT Enterprise Technologies AI team, Information Security Office, SRC staff, and other key stakeholders.

This is a full time fixed-term position for a 3 year term. It is an onsite or hybrid position.

US citizenship or permanent residency required. This position cannot sponsor a work permit now or in the future.

Responsibilities

AI tool evaluation, approval and communication (about 50%)

In collaboration with UIT ET and other stakeholders help shape how AI tools for research are evaluated and approved at Stanford, participating in the process for identifying, evaluating, and approving new tools in a timely manner.
Work with the research community to identify, and prioritize, new AI tools to evaluate (eg. coding assistants, literature and data-analysis tools, agent platforms, research-specific AI services, etc.)
Work with the AI team in University IT’s Enterprise Technology to evaluate AI tools, publish the approved-tools list, create and update documentation of the approved AI tools for research, as well as communicate results of evaluations to the relevant research communities at Stanford.
In collaboration with UIT ET shepherd selected tools through Stanford’s security, privacy, legal, regulatory, and procurement review.
Communicate approved tools to the research community: plain-language guidance on what each tool may be used for, announcements of new approvals and changes, and answers to researcher questions.
Collect feedback from the research community and usage data after approval, and recommend renewals, changes or retirement of tools.

Research consultation (about 20%)

Meet with researchers to understand their questions and data, advise which approved tools to use as well as take in their requests of new tools needing evaluation. Build an evaluation request pipeline.
Help researchers apply approved AI tools in research.
Advise on sound and responsible practice of utilizing AI tools in research: evaluation and validity, reproducibility, sensitive data (HIPAA, FERPA, CUI), IRB considerations and licensing.
Participate in fielding SRC tickets and requests from the research community.

Deploying & Evaluating AI tools on HPC platforms (about 15%)

Help researchers move AI work onto our HPC systems: accounts, Jupyter and Open OnDemand, environments, Slurm jobs and data transfer.
Troubleshoot common AI workflow problems and work with other SRC staff to resolve issues researchers encounter.
Connect researchers to campus, cloud, and national resources (NAIRR Pilot, ACCESS).

Training, communications, and documentation (about 15%)

Run workshops and office hours, focused on approved AI tools and on running AI work on HPC. Communicate approved AI tools to researcher community members.
Update and publish up to date information about approved AI tools for research. Write how-to guides and examples to go with approved tools.

Required Qualifications

Education and experience

Master’s degree in a research field that uses computation (any discipline, including data science, statistics, computer science, the sciences, social sciences or engineering) plus 2 years of relevant experience; or a PhD; or a bachelor’s plus 4 years; or an equivalent combination.
Has applied machine learning or AI to real research or analysis problems, end to end: from framing the question through evaluating and reporting results.

Technical Skills

Broad, hands-on knowledge of the current AI tool landscape for research (chat and coding assistants, literature and data-analysis tools, agent platforms) and experience evaluating AI tools and platforms.
Understanding of how AI tools handle data: retention, use of inputs for training, access controls, and integrations.
Working knowledge of LLMs and generative AI for research: eg. prompting, API use, open-weight models, autonomous agents, model training, external data integration such as RAG, tool use/function calling, web search integration, etc.
Comfortable on Linux and able to run batch and interactive work on an HPC cluster (Slurm preferred), or learn quickly with training.

Professional (“soft”) Skills

Excellent listener and translator: understands a researcher’s field and goals and explains AI options in their terms.
Writes clear, accurate evaluations and plain-language guidance that turn approval decisions into helpful documentation.
Works effectively across organizational boundaries, building trust across diverse stakeholder groups with a goal of moving processes forward to support research teams.
Good judgment and candor: will say when a tool is not ready, not safe for certain data, or not the right fit.
Organized and persistent: tracks many tools, reviews and requests at once and follows through.
Curious and self-directed learner in a fast-moving field, committed to welcoming support for researchers of all backgrounds.

Experience

Preferred qualifications

PhD, or substantial research experience as a graduate student, postdoc or research staff member, using AI in a domain science, social science, humanities or health field.
Experience evaluating, piloting or rolling out software or AI tools in a university or other large organization.
Experience working with central IT, information security, privacy or procurement on technology reviews.
2+ years as a research computing facilitator, data science consultant, or in a researcher-facing role in higher education.

Technical Skills

Experience with one or more application areas such as: scientific foundation models, NLP and text-as-data, computer vision and imaging, time series, or tabular data.
Building LLM applications for research: eg., RAG, embeddings and vector databases, structured extraction, evaluation of LLM outputs, agent frameworks.
Open OnDemand, JupyterHub and containers (Apptainer) from a user’s point of view.
Familiarity with AI governance, research ethics and sensitive-data environments.

Professional (“soft”) Skills

Consulting skills: scopes engagements, sets expectations and follows up.
Experience building communities, such as user groups, hackathons or communities of practice.
Comfortable presenting to a variety of audiences: faculty, students, staff, department chairs, and leadership.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Core Duties
:

Researcher Engagement:

Lead collaboration with cross-functional technical teams, faculty and researchers to understand their research goals and identify technical obstacles and solutions for highly complex research questions.
Assist researchers in the identification of appropriate computational platforms (locally and externally); the tuning, debugging, optimization, and enhancement of their existing algorithms on mid-scale HPC, cloud computing, and national facilities.
Advise researchers in the best use of a broad set of cyberinfrastructure systems, tools, and software.
Build a deep understanding of specific research activities associated with strategic campus priorities.
Regularly attend research meetings to develop both formal and informal pathways for regular exchanges of information.
Develop and surface metrics to demonstrate effectiveness and impact on researcher productivity and success as a result of engagements.

Solutions Development:

Formulate complex and innovative technical strategies and engineer them to completion to achieve unique research objectives and overcome any research challenges, using external vendors as needed.
Lead the development of frameworks that assist researchers in analyzing and visualizing data to uncover insights and support research findings. Consult on the creation and management of large, variable datasets in order to enable their preparation and use in research for modeling and analysis.
Execute technical solutions to meet the most complex research needs, including machine learning algorithms, text and image processing techniques, API programming, custom full-stack applications, automated web scraping, and crowdsourcing pipelines, to inform research findings. Facilitate the design, debugging, and automating/scripting of novel complex research workflows with researchers. Develop enhancements to workflows.
Synthesize complex patterns in research and evaluate potential platforms, including meeting with representatives from emerging industries and analyzing tools and systems through the lens of academic research, spanning Artificial Intelligence, Big Data and Cloud Technologies.
Continuously adapt to and formulate solutions using evolving technologies and methodologies to accelerate research development and enable new research frontiers. Leverage leading-edge technical knowledge and interpersonal skills to support and enhance academic research.
Ensure the feasibility of support and security of such solutions, and compliance with applicable local, campus or national policies, practices and regulations.

Documentation/Training:

Collaborate with research leads and teams to research and develop efforts to enhance the team's capabilities in research support, including training sessions, testing new data collection methods, and staying abreast of relevant literature.
Participate and present at industry conferences and meetings to understand the latest academic research papers and computer source code. Replicate results from diverse fields as needed.
Build advanced curriculum and teach workshops on topics such as software porting techniques, parallelization and optimization methodologies, computational platforms, and data management, ensuring that those workshops are aligned with unit goals, referenced technologies are supported and supportable, materials are vetted collaboratively by peers and team, and all sessions are evaluated by participants.
Lead the development and delivery of documentation and training for faculty and research staff.
Document all interactions, solutions and approaches discussed with researcher-facing and systems-facing peers.

Partnership/Collaboration:

Connect and coordinate interactions between researchers and technology providers, management and technology partners. Connect research teams with external experts, resources and local team members, peers and management as needed to facilitate solution development.
Work closely and collaboratively with peers to ensure that proposed solutions do not adversely affect overall system performance and that solutions are consistent with local policies.
Provide regular communications to systems and software/data professionals and ensure management awareness of proposed initiatives and approaches.

Project Team Lead:

This role may occasionally lead functional teams in the development and execution of projects. Provide mentorship, coaching, and leadership to team members as needed.
Provide guidance and direction to more junior members of the team on projects.

Master's degree in computer science, data science, statistics, or a related field

jobs.description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

Can you bring up a GPU cluster, build a lab around it, and teach it to a room of engineers? NVIDIA's Education Services is hiring a Senior Technical Trainer and Content Developer to build and teach our compute curriculum for AI factories. We train the partner and customer engineers who bring NVIDIA AI clusters up and keep them running. Our courses cover deploying, operating and troubleshooting AI factories: NVIDIA DGX and HGX systems, cluster bring-up and validation, cluster management and scheduling, and GPU health and performance. This is a builder's role as much as a teaching one: development carries real weight. We build with AI tools every day, and we want engineers who do the same!

What You'll Be Doing

We design, build and maintain our own courses: slides, lab guides, demos and assessments. Our hands-on labs run on on-prem GPU clusters and in simulated and emulated environments. We keep them reliable for every class. Working with subject-matter experts, we turn new products and reference designs into training, often before formal documentation exists. AI coding assistants and agents help us prototype labs, automate environments and draft content, within NVIDIA's guidelines. We verify their output with an engineer's rigor.

We also lead instructor-led training, in person and remotely, and enable partner instructors to deliver our courses. In class, we teach, run live demos on real and simulated systems, and resolve lab issues as they come up. Expect up to 20% travel to customer sites and events such as NVIDIA GTC. You will own this work end to end, from first prototype to classroom.

What We Need To See

We are looking for an engineer with deep technical experience and strong self-learning skills, who teaches clearly in English and writes well. Prior training, enablement, documentation or mentoring work all count. We also expect the basics of AI: training and inference, neural networks, deep learning, and why GPUs matter.

Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
8+ years of hands-on data center experience deploying or operating HPC clusters or bringing up AI clusters, including troubleshooting them.
Hardware depth: installing, administering and diagnosing servers and GPUs, and carrying out maintenance work such as firmware upgrades.
Advanced Linux administration, with practical experience in cluster storage and performance optimization.
Basic TCP/IP networking, cloud and Kubernetes knowledge, and the IT fluency to debug a lab end to end.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Intensive, demonstrable work with AI tools such as Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and open models, including agent skills and workflows.
Hands-on labs, simulated or emulated, built for technical audiences, with DevOps and platform skills for lab automation: Git, Docker and containers, Kubernetes (for example Amazon EKS), Argo CD, Terraform, PostgreSQL, Bash or Python.
NVIDIA DGX or HGX deployments and AI factory build-outs, reference designs and product lines.
NVIDIA Mission Control, Run:ai and Slurm, GPU monitoring tools (DCGM, NVSM, nvidia-smi), benchmarks such as HPL, and AI workloads at scale.
NVIDIA professional-level certifications in AI infrastructure or operations, and NVIDIA AI Enterprise software.

Are you ready to build the training behind AI factories? Come build it with us!

Can you help build the physical infrastructure behind an AI data center and teach the engineers and partners who bring it to life? NVIDIA’s Education Services team is hiring a Senior Technical Trainer and Content Developer to build and teach our AI data center curriculum. We train the partner and customer teams who turn AI data center designs into deployed infrastructure. Our courses cover mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems; power and cooling; fiber cabling; equipment installation; and the coordination required to bring these systems together. This is a builder’s role as much as a teaching one: field experience, practical judgment, and content development carry real weight.

What You’ll Be Doing

We design, build, and maintain our own courses: slides, lab guides, demos, and assessments. You’ll turn physical deployment practices into hands-on learning, including equipment installation, rack deployment, cabling, infrastructure readiness checks, and troubleshooting. Working with subject-matter experts, you’ll translate new products, reference designs, and DSX concepts into practical training, often before formal documentation exists.
Develop curriculum around AI data center power and cooling requirements, including calculations for electrical loads, rack power density, cooling capacity, and liquid-cooling flow requirements. You’ll help learners understand how these requirements influence facility readiness, equipment placement, installation sequencing, and deployment decisions.
Bring experience leading deployment teams in the field and coordinating work across disciplines. You’ll work with our partner ecosystem—including power and cooling suppliers, construction firms, installation contractors, and energy providers—to reflect real deployment practices, dependencies, and lessons learned in our training.
We also lead instructor-led training, in person and remotely, and enable partner instructors to deliver our courses. In class, you’ll teach, lead practical demonstrations, and resolve lab issues as they come up. We use AI coding assistants and agents to help develop content, prototype learning activities, and automate supporting workflows within NVIDIA’s guidelines. We validate their output for technical accuracy and practical use.
Expect up to 20% travel to customer sites, partner facilities, and events such as NVIDIA GTC. You will own this work end to end, from first prototype to classroom.

What We Need To See

We are looking for a technically strong builder with deep field experience and strong self-learning skills, who teaches clearly in English and writes well. Prior training, enablement, documentation, or mentoring work all count.

12+ years of hands-on experience building, installing, or commissioning physical data center infrastructure, including high-density environments.
Practical knowledge of MEP systems and how electrical distribution, cooling, liquid-cooling plumbing, and facility infrastructure support AI data center deployments.
Physical installation experience with racks, servers, power distribution equipment, cooling connections, and fiber cabling, including cable routing, labeling, testing, and installation quality checks.
Familiarity with AI data center architectures and DSX concepts, with an understanding of how compute requirements translate into physical infrastructure needs.
Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, construction management, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Direct experience delivering high-density AI data centers, liquid-cooled deployments, or NVIDIA AI factory buildouts.
Experience applying NVIDIA DSX concepts and reference designs to deployment planning, infrastructure sizing, or technical training.
Hands-on experience with liquid-cooling infrastructure, including coolant distribution units, manifolds, piping connections, and leak testing.
Demonstrable work with AI tools such as Claude, Codex, Gemini, and open models to develop and validate technical content, including agent skills and workflows.
Familiarity with NVIDIA DGX and HGX systems and their physical installation, power, cooling, and connectivity requirements.

Are you ready to build the training behind AI data centers? Come build it with us!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary range for this position is 210,000 USD – 403,000 USD.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 28, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.
